title: Chapter 11: Switching and Virtual LANs
summary: How switches learn and forward frames, how VLANs split broadcast domains, how 802.1Q tagging and STP keep trunked networks working, and how port security, QoS, and PoE fit in.

visuals.title: Switch learning and flooding
visuals.description: A switch learns source MAC addresses, forwards known destinations, and floods unknown ones. (Review questions 1, 2, 8)

visuals.title: VLANs and broadcast domains
visuals.description: Assign ports to VLANs and see which hosts receive a broadcast. (Review questions 7, 8, 10)

visuals.title: Static vs dynamic VLANs
visuals.description: Compare administrator-assigned ports with VMPS lookups by MAC address. (Review questions 9, 11)

visuals.title: Segmenting with an SVI and ACLs
visuals.description: Test traffic flows for an R&D VLAN and see why the other options fall short. (Review question 15)

visuals.title: VTP and protected VLANs
visuals.description: Propagate a VLAN from a VTP server and try deleting VLAN 1. (Review questions 14, 18, 20)

visuals.title: Access ports, trunks, and the native VLAN
visuals.description: Step a frame across a trunk and see where tags are added and removed. (Review questions 12, 17, 19)

visuals.title: 802.1Q frame tag
visuals.description: Inspect each field of a tagged frame, including TPID, CoS, and VLAN ID. (Review questions 3, 4, 16)

visuals.title: STP root bridge election
visuals.description: Change priorities and see which switch becomes the root. (Review question 5)

visuals.title: STP port states
visuals.description: Watch a port move from blocking to forwarding over 50 seconds. (Written lab 7, 8)

visuals.title: Port security
visuals.description: Limit a port to two devices and see what happens to the third. (Review questions 6, 13)

visuals.title: Hubs, bridges, switches, and routers
visuals.description: Compare hubs, bridges, switches, and routers by layer, latency, and domains. (Review question 1, 10)

visuals.title: Broadcast and collision domains with VLANs
visuals.description: Add VLANs and switch duplex mode to see how broadcast and collision domain counts change. (Review question 10)

visuals.title: QoS marking by layer
visuals.description: Compare CoS, ToS, and DiffServ by layer, and see which CoS value maps to which queue. (Review question 3, written lab 10)

visuals.title: Choosing a trunking protocol
visuals.description: Choose each switch vendor and protocol to see whether ISL or 802.1Q fits. (Review question 4)

visuals.title: Power over Ethernet budget
visuals.description: Match a PoE device to 802.3af or 802.3at and check the port power budget. (Written lab 5)
